A mortar left mid-grind, the pestle standing upright in a paste of crushed nightbell that is throwing slow green sparks up toward the ceiling, a folded leaf tucked beneath the mortar's lip to keep it from walking across the counter.

A copper still dripping liquid light into a thimble-flask, each drop flaring white as it lands and settling to deep amber, a neat tally of river pebbles counting the drops along the counter edge, a saucer catching what spills.

A tincture settling in a tall glass column, its sediment falling upward in a bright slow cloud of copper motes, a stone laid flat across the top to hold the stopper down against whatever is pushing from within.

A poultice half-spread on a square of linen, the linen's edges already knitting themselves closed around it in slow neat stitches, a second strip of linen folded and waiting beside it, a thimble set out at the corner ready.

A small wooden press screwed part-way down over a bundle of stems, green light beading along the lip of it and running in thin threads to the counter, a saucer positioned to catch the threads before they reach the edge.

A bundle of dried stems tied with cord and hung upside-down, already budding again at three points, the new buds pale and faintly luminous, a second length of cord coiled below it on the hook as though anticipated.

A stoppered jar cooling in a basin, the water around it frozen in perfect concentric rings outward to the basin's rim, the stopper vibrating very slightly, a cork already chewed sitting beside the basin as a spare.

A bottle half-decanted into three small cups, each cup holding a different colour from the same slow-pouring stream — the first deep green, the second pale gold, the third a bruised and luminous violet — the bottle tilted and resting on a folded leaf.

A sieve of seed-heads with all the chaff drifting upward instead of down, collecting in a soft pale cloud at the ceiling above it, a thimble set beneath the sieve to gather the seeds that do fall through.

A honey jar tipped on its side, a slow golden thread running from its mouth across the counter to the edge and stopping there in a perfect hovering bead, a saucer placed just below the bead in case it decides to fall.

A paper twist half-folded around a pinch of small bright seeds, several of which have lifted off the counter and are hanging in a loose cluster an inch above the paper, a stone set at the twist's corner to anchor what remains.

A kettle on its trivet steaming a single perfect ring of vapour that hangs in the air above it unbroken, a second ring just forming at the spout, a folded leaf placed over the trivet's handle to mark its readiness.

A rose-petal salve in a wide clay pot, three new buds sprouting along the rim of it, their petals beginning to open and curl into the salve itself, a saucer of clean water set beside the pot as though offered in welcome.

Two slender wands of pale glass laid across a bowl of still water, a bright spark travelling slowly from one tip across the gap to the other, the water in the bowl reflecting the spark doubled, a chewed cork resting at the bowl's edge.
A candle-flame bent sideways over a shallow bowl and held there, the wax running away down the far side instead, a saucer waiting at the correct side already waxed with prior catchings.

A funnel of folded birch-bark pouring a thin stream of starlight into a bottle already full of it, the bottle deepening rather than overflowing, a tally of five small pebbles counting the funnels used lined along the counter behind it.

A bowl of dark water with a root soaking in it, a thread of white blossom growing along the bowl's inner rim away from the root as though exploring, a folded leaf pressed flat over half the bowl to shelter what blossoms.

A phial standing open on the sill, a thread of rainwater coming in through the wall and finding it with perfect aim, the phial filling in slow clear increments, a thimble placed beside it to accept any overflow.

A drying tray where half the petals have turned luminous, glowing pale gold as they lie flat, the other half still drying and ordinary, the border between the two moving very slowly across the tray, a stone at the tray's corner keeping it level.

A twig-and-acorn balance with one pan holding a thin moonbeam and the other a pinch of gold spores, the moonbeam winning and the spore-pan lifting gently, a thimble set below the higher pan ready to receive when the spores tip.

A mortar of crushed berries whose purple stain is spreading slowly outward across the stone into the precise shape of a many-lobed leaf, the pestle laid to the side, a folded leaf placed beneath the mortar to mark the counter beneath it clean.

A crucible set to cool on the counter, a small bead of amber resin at its centre holding a tiny frozen flame inside it, the flame entirely still, a chewed cork lying beside the crucible as though the stopper arrived early.

A cup of steeping herbs with a single large leaf circling slowly on its own against the current of the water, the steam rising in a thin clockwise curl, a second empty cup standing ready beside it with a stone inside to hold it from sliding.

A jar of luminous spores with the lid set aside and a slow bright spiral of them climbing out and spreading along the ceiling in a widening arc, a second empty jar already open beside it as though the first will need decanting soon.

A small press half-turned over a mound of bluebell root, moonlight pooling in the groove at its base where it waits to be collected, a thimble-flask positioned directly beneath the groove's end, a tally of three pebbles marking the presses already completed nearby.
